_comment: Generated from each widget's settings.json and core/analytics.settings.json by widgets/tests/check.rs - rewrite it with `UPDATE_CONFIG_EXAMPLE=1 cargo test --test check generated_config_example_matches_widget_settings`. Copy to config.json (git-ignored) or ~/.config/opscope/config.json. Every key is optional; anything omitted keeps that section's default.

agent_usage._comment:
Reads local agent state, plus remaining quota from each agent's own host with that agent's own credential. Grok's quota call is on by default and may start the Grok CLI to refresh its token; turn grok_ping off to keep those off.

Empty agents discovers whatever this machine has; naming them instead fixes the set and the order and turns discovery off. exclude_agents drops one either way.

A leftover section still named usage is read as this one, and the pane says so.
agent_usage._auto_detect_agent_comment:
Show whatever agents this machine turns out to have.

On, which is what has always happened when no set was named — it was simply spelt as an empty list, which nothing on screen could name.

While it is on, an agent's tab stays hidden until detection says that agent is present, and agents below is ignored; exclude_agents still applies, so dropping one does not mean naming all the others.

Turn it off to show exactly the agents picked, in that order, including while a read is still in flight.

Leave the key out entirely and the old rule decides: a named list wins, an empty one discovers.
agent_usage._agents_comment: Agent names to show, in the order given; empty discovers whatever local state this machine has. Pick from the list rather than typing: a name that is not one of those listed is not an error, it is simply an agent that never appears.
agent_usage._exclude_agents_comment: Agents to leave out, applied either way — to the ones discovered automatically and to a list named by hand. Picked from the same list, so an exclusion cannot be spelt wrongly and silently do nothing.
agent_usage._refresh_comment: Seconds between local state and allowed quota refreshes.
agent_usage._work_days_per_week_comment:
Days a week you actually work, counted from Monday: 5 is Monday to Friday, 6 adds Saturday.

The pace figure and the mark on every quota bar then measure a window by the work time gone rather than the clock, so a weekly quota is all but spent by Friday night instead of showing a weekend of headroom you will not use.

Monthly and billing-cycle windows count the work days actually in that cycle, so there is no separate monthly setting. Windows of a day or less, like the five-hour session or a daily quota, stay on the clock. 7, the default, is the clock throughout.
agent_usage._rates_comment:
OPTIONAL override, in US$ per million tokens, keyed by model. Published list prices ship in the code, dated on screen, so nothing here is needed to price a known model.

Enter opens the rate card: the models you have set something on, or all of them when you have none, with tab to switch and typing to search. Enter on a model lists its priced kinds — input, output, cache_read, cache_write, cache_write_1h — with the published price as the default, and d on the card drops a model back to list prices.

Set only the numbers you want to change: config wins per kind, so the rest keep tracking the shipped card and still get a vendor's correction. A model is yours only when it holds a number; opening one writes nothing.

Use this to correct a stale price, to price a model the card does not carry, or to apply your own negotiated rates.

Reasoning tokens are not a kind: vendors count them inside output, so pricing them again would charge them twice. Longest matching model name wins, and '*' overrides these kinds for any model no other key names.
agent_usage._plan_cost_comment:
What each subscription costs you per month, per agent, in US$. A flat monthly figure — the per-token prices are `rates`, which is a different setting.

Nothing ships here: plans vary by tier and region, and no invoice is on this machine.

Set one and METERED gains 'the plan saves' — the month's cost at list prices against what you actually pay.
agent_usage._antigravity_remote_comment:
Antigravity publishes its quota two ways: a language server that runs inside the app, and Google, which serves the same summary on the endpoint the tier already comes from.

The local one is preferred and this only decides whether the remote one may be asked when the app is shut. On by default — it is the same host and the same credential the tier request already uses.

Turn it off and the quota is absent whenever Antigravity is closed; the tab then says so, and names this key.
agent_usage._antigravity_start_comment:
Whether the widget may run the `agy` CLI to read the quota, when no running app answers. On by default. It is your own CLI, already installed and signed in.

On 1.1.11 or later it runs `agy -p /usage`, which is a command and not a prompt, so it spends no tokens, and it is the only source left with the Gemini group: Google's summary has only the Claude and GPT-OSS one.

It runs in a private empty directory with the browser openers stubbed out, so it can never pop a sign-in page, and its whole process group is killed as soon as the reading is taken. Older builds are started under a pseudo-terminal instead and killed by pid.

A CLI you started yourself is found by the ordinary local probe long before this runs, so this can never shut one of yours down.

Off means the quota comes from Google alone, without the Gemini group, and lasts an hour past the last time Antigravity ran, which is the token's life. grok_ping is the other setting that may start a CLI.
agent_usage._grok_ping_comment:
Grok is the only agent with no live quota: its figures come from the log its own CLI writes, so they move only when you use Grok on this machine.

Turn grok_ping on to ask x.ai instead, using the token the CLI leaves in ~/.grok/auth.json. That also runs the Grok CLI once after a session goes quiet, which is what refreshes the token — without it the asking works until the token lapses and then silently stops.

On by default: the request goes to the endpoint the Grok CLI itself bills through, with that CLI's own token, and the alternative is a figure that moves only when you use Grok on this machine and is marked cached.

Turn it off to keep the widget from talking to x.ai or starting the CLI; the tab then says so and names this key.
agent_usage._grok_ping_minutes_comment:
Minutes between enabled Grok quota polls. Thirty is the most it will take.

A reading older than thirty-one minutes is drawn with the cached mark, so the ceiling sits a minute under it and the freshest answer the widget can hold is always inside the window that judges it.

A larger number in a hand-edited file is clamped, and the tab says the interval actually used.
agent_usage._notion_token_comment:
Notion AI's usage allowance, on Business and Enterprise workspaces: a rolling six-hour window and the billing period.

Notion publishes no API for it, so the widget asks the one its web app uses, with your token_v2 session cookie.

1. Sign in at app.notion.com and open developer tools.
2. Open the cookies and copy the value of token_v2.
3. Paste it here. A whole Cookie header copied from a request works too.

It is a full sign-in to your Notion account, not a scoped key, so keep this file chmod 600. The widget never reads it out of a browser. Empty reads the variable named in notion_token_env; empty there too and Notion has no tab.
agent_usage._notion_token_env_comment: Environment variable holding the token_v2 cookie when notion_token is empty.
agent_usage._notion_workspace_comment: The Notion workspace to report, by id, with or without its dashes. Empty picks the first on a Business or Enterprise plan, since only those carry an allowance. An id the account cannot see falls back to that choice.
agent_usage._perplexity_token_comment:
Perplexity's weekly limit, credits and billing. Perplexity publishes no API for them and an API key (pplx-...) cannot read them, so the widget asks the endpoints perplexity.ai's own usage page uses, with your web session cookie.

To find it:

1. Sign in at perplexity.ai and open developer tools: F12, or Cmd-Option-I on a Mac. Safari needs Settings, Advanced, Show features for web developers turned on first.
2. Open the cookies for https://www.perplexity.ai: the Application tab in Chrome, Edge, Arc or Brave, the Storage tab in Firefox and Safari.
3. Copy the Value of __Secure-next-auth.session-token. The console cannot read it, since the cookie is HttpOnly. If it is split into .0 and .1 cookies, copy the whole cookie request header from a request to www.perplexity.ai that includes the session cookie, in the Network tab instead.
4. Paste it here.

It is a full sign-in to your Perplexity account, not a scoped key, so keep this file chmod 600. The widget never reads it out of a browser. Empty reads the variable named in perplexity_token_env; empty there too and Perplexity has no tab.
agent_usage._perplexity_token_env_comment:
The name of the environment variable to read the Perplexity session cookie from, for keeping it out of this file.

It is read only when perplexity_token is empty: when both are set, perplexity_token wins, so empty that field to use the variable.

Change this only to use a variable name other than PERPLEXITY_SESSION_TOKEN.
agent_usage._devin_token_comment:
Devin's bearer token for the daily and weekly quota. Copy it yourself; the widget never reads a browser.

It is sent only to app.devin.ai, and only while Devin is one of the agents shown. Keep this file chmod 600.

Empty reads the variable named in devin_token_env, DEVIN_AUTHORIZATION when that variable is empty too, and then the credential a signed-in Devin CLI stored - devin_cli_credentials switches that last step off.
agent_usage._devin_token_env_comment: Environment variable holding the Devin bearer token when devin_token is empty.
agent_usage._devin_org_comment:
The Devin organization the quota is read for. An internal id (org- or org_) is sent as the path and as x-cog-org-id. Anything else is the slug under org/.

Empty reads the org the signed-in Devin CLI named in its config.json, while devin_cli_credentials is on. Devin has no tab until both this and a token are set.
agent_usage._devin_cli_credentials_comment:
Whether a signed-in Devin CLI's own files may supply the token and organization when neither is set above. On by default: it is what lets Devin appear with no settings at all.

The files are the CLI's credentials.toml (windsurf_api_key) and config.json (devin.org_id) under the usual data/config roots.

Off means a token and an org must come from the fields and variables above, exactly as before.
agent_usage._factory_api_key_comment: Factory API key for the Droid tab. Sent only to api.factory.ai (and app.factory.ai when the API host does not answer), and only while Droid is one of the agents shown. Keep this file chmod 600. Empty reads the variable named in factory_api_key_env, then the FACTORY_API_KEY line in ~/.factory/.env.
agent_usage._factory_api_key_env_comment: Environment variable holding the Factory API key when factory_api_key is empty. ~/.factory/.env is read after that.
agent_usage._claude_config_dirs_comment:
Claude Code config directories to read.

1. Type a path in the empty box to add a directory.
2. Press enter on its row to open it as its own screen and give it the name its tab should read.
3. Press enter on the empty box to open that screen blank for a new entry.

Unset or empty is ["~/.claude"] — today's single CLAUDE tab / CLAUDE group. When the list is set, those directories are watched in this order and no others. ~ is expanded.

A second Max lives in its own directory; two or more become extra tabs and extra [+] groups titled with each entry's label (not CLAUDE) — the label written, or the directory's own name with any leading dot dropped.

~/.claude is always CLAUDE: it carries no label, and a label written on it is ignored rather than refused, so it survives being moved down the list. No other entry may take that name either; a second one asking for it becomes claude-2. They are never merged into one bar.

With one directory the label is unused: the tab and the group read CLAUDE, so a label set today survives a second directory added later. Two entries wanting the same name are told apart with -2 on the second. The same path cannot be listed twice under two names; remove the row it is on first.

$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CLI Proxy, ~/.claude-* scanning, Desktop and VS Code are out of scope.

analytics._comment: Counts of which binaries are started, so the project can be supported and so we can see which widgets are used. The same event goes to the Vercel Analytics and Google Analytics this build was released with. Empty settings below mean those built-in destinations; set one to send somewhere else instead. A build from source has none built in. Collect URLs must be https. An event carries the widget or launcher name and that a start happened. The first choice also says opted in or opted out, and the time of that choice. Nothing in an event is a hostname, an account, the contents of this file, or an identity. `enabled` is not listed here on purpose: with it absent, the next interactive launch asks once and writes true (accept) or false (decline) itself, so a copy of this example never turns counting on without that question. Edit `enabled` afterwards to change the choice; it is not asked again.
analytics._vercel_url_comment: Collect URL for Vercel Web Analytics, scheme and host included; https only, anything else skips Vercel. Empty uses the one this build was released with; a build from source has none, and then Vercel is skipped. The path is that project's insights event route. The id below is sent with the event when it is set; it is not a token.
analytics._vercel_analytics_id_comment: Vercel Web Analytics id, sent with each event when set. Empty still sends when vercel_url is set, which is enough when the URL itself identifies the project. Not a token.
analytics._ga_measurement_id_comment: GA4 measurement id. Empty uses the one this build was released with; a build from source has none, and then Google Analytics is skipped unless this and the secret below are set.
analytics._ga_api_secret_comment: GA4 Measurement Protocol api secret. Empty uses the one this build was released with. Keep this file chmod 600.

clocks._cities_comment:
World clocks as [label, IANA timezone] pairs. A row may also be [label, zone, latitude, longitude]; those two numbers opt that city into its own current-conditions glyph, and nothing else does — the label and the timezone are never looked up.

The search list writes pairs, so coordinates are added by editing the row. A zone the database does not know is dropped without a word.

The order here is ignored — the pane sorts west to east by each zone's current offset, with the label breaking ties, so the rows read as a map.
clocks._weather_latitude_comment:
Latitude, in degrees from -90 to 90, of the one place whose current weather is shown. Null leaves weather off.

Zero is the equator, so it is a real place once you set it — an unset field stays null rather than zero. Set longitude as well; one without the other is reported on the pane and not fetched.
clocks._weather_longitude_comment: Longitude, in degrees from -180 to 180, of that same place. Null leaves weather off. The widget does not guess a coordinate from a city name or from the machine.
clocks._weather_label_comment: Optional name drawn beside the temperature. Empty shows the conditions without a place name. The coordinates are what is fetched; this text is only a label.
clocks._work_start_hour_comment: Local 24-hour clock hour when the work day begins.
clocks._work_end_hour_comment: Local 24-hour clock hour when the work day ends.
clocks._show_hints_comment: Whether the pomodoro key hints sit under the panel. Visible by default: the hints are how the keys are found in the first place, and starting hidden means a reader has to already know the key that reveals them. [?] toggles it live.
clocks._work_days_comment: Which days count as working days, as names (sun, mon, ...) or numbers. Drives the working-day shading.
clocks._pomodoro_enabled_comment: Whether the pomodoro starts enabled when clocks launches.
clocks._pomodoro_sessions_before_long_break_com: Completed focus sessions before a long break.
clocks._pomodoro_bell_comment: Whether a terminal bell sounds when a phase ends.
clocks._pomodoro_notify_comment: Whether a desktop notification is attempted when a phase ends.
clocks._pomodoro_flash_comment: Whether the pane flashes when a phase ends.
clocks._pomodoro_flash_rgb_comment: Flash colour as three red, green, blue values.

disk._comment: Filesystem space and inodes. Linux reads /proc/self/mountinfo and statvfs; macOS reads getmntinfo. Pseudo filesystems, bind mounts and read-only mounts are hidden because none of them can fill.
disk._refresh_comment: Seconds between samples. Minimum 0.5. -n SECONDS on the command line overrides this for one run.
disk._hide_mounts_comment: Mount points to hide. An entry is an exact path, or a prefix of every mount under it when it ends in /. The entry / hides only the root mount; a prefix of / would hide every absolute path.
disk._hide_devices_comment: Whole-disk names to hide, matched exactly. An idle disk with no reads and no writes since boot is already hidden until v is pressed; this list hides a disk whether or not it is idle.
disk._warn_percent_comment: Percent used at which the bar starts to leave green. At and below this the bar stays quiet.
disk._alert_percent_comment: Percent used at which the bar is fully hot. Between warn_percent and this it climbs in a straight line.
disk._window_hours_comment: How many hours of this widget's own samples the window rate, the FULL IN column and the filesystem trace start from. 6, 12 or 24. w on the pane cycles the same three for this session and does not write the choice back.

github._comment: token: a CLASSIC PAT with repo + read:org — fine-grained tokens reach only one org each, and this board spans several. The API is called directly, so the gh CLI is not needed. Keep this file chmod 600.
github._token_comment: Classic GitHub token; leave empty to read the named environment variable.
github._token_env_comment: Environment variable that holds the GitHub token.
github._enterprise_hostname_comment: Web hostname of a GitHub Enterprise Cloud tenant (for example acme.ghe.com). A *.ghe.com host is called at api.<host>. Empty reads the variable enterprise_hostname_env names, if any; otherwise github.com.
github._enterprise_hostname_env_comment: Name of an environment variable to read when enterprise_hostname is empty, for example GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_HOSTNAME. Empty reads none. This is a variable name, never a hostname.
github._accounts_comment: GitHub users or organizations to include; empty discovers the viewer and their organizations.
github._window_days_comment: Days included in delivery charts and summaries.

github_actions._comment:
Uses this widget's own token, then the variable token_env names, which defaults to $GITHUB_TOKEN. It does not read any other widget's section: a token here and a different one under `github` is an ordinary thing to want, and borrowing would run this widget on a credential its own settings screen never showed.

Empty accounts discovers the viewer login and every org they belong to.

Empty repos means recently-pushed repos that have workflow files, capped at max_repos per owner so one busy org cannot hide personal — never every repo the token can see. The screen names the cap.
github_actions._token_comment: This widget's GitHub token. Empty falls through to the variable token_env names, not to another widget's token.
github_actions._token_env_comment: Which environment variable holds the token, when `token` is empty. Defaults to GITHUB_TOKEN. This is a variable name, never a credential.
github_actions._enterprise_hostname_comment: Web hostname of a GitHub Enterprise Cloud tenant (for example acme.ghe.com). A *.ghe.com host is called at api.<host>. Empty reads the variable enterprise_hostname_env names, if any; otherwise github.com.
github_actions._enterprise_hostname_env_comment: Name of an environment variable to read when enterprise_hostname is empty, for example GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_HOSTNAME. Empty reads none. This is a variable name, never a hostname.
github_actions._accounts_comment: GitHub users or organizations to inspect; empty discovers the viewer and their organizations.
github_actions._repos_comment: Explicit owner/repository names; empty discovers recently pushed repositories with workflows.
github_actions._window_hours_comment: Hours of workflow runs included in summaries.
github_actions._max_repos_comment: Maximum discovered repositories inspected per account.
github_actions._pushed_days_comment: How recently a repository must have been pushed to qualify for discovery.

github_prs._comment:
Uses this widget's own token, then the variable token_env names, which defaults to $GITHUB_TOKEN. It does not read any other widget's section.

Each source is one GitHub search; results are pooled and de-duplicated, because GitHub search has no OR. @mine expands to every org you belong to plus your own account.
github_prs._token_comment: This widget's GitHub token. Empty falls through to the variable token_env names, not to another widget's token.
github_prs._token_env_comment: Which environment variable holds the token, when `token` is empty. Defaults to GITHUB_TOKEN. This is a variable name, never a credential.
github_prs._enterprise_hostname_comment: Web hostname of a GitHub Enterprise Cloud tenant (for example acme.ghe.com). A *.ghe.com host is called at api.<host>. Empty reads the variable enterprise_hostname_env names, if any; otherwise github.com.
github_prs._enterprise_hostname_env_comment: Name of an environment variable to read when enterprise_hostname is empty, for example GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_HOSTNAME. Empty reads none. This is a variable name, never a hostname.
github_prs._sources_comment: Named GitHub search queries pooled and de-duplicated into the follow-up queue.
github_prs._limit_comment: How many results to ask GitHub for per page. Not a cap on what is shown: paging continues until every search is exhausted. A smaller page is slower to finish and far likelier to be served when GitHub search is having a slow minute; a round that is refused backs off to 10 on its own.

google_analytics._comment: GA4 properties through a Google service-account key: realtime against a baseline this widget records itself, today against the same weekday, key events, organic landing pages and movers. Setup on Google's side is docs/google-setup.md. Keep the key file and config.json chmod 600.
google_analytics._credentials_comment:
The service-account JSON key itself: paste the whole downloaded file here. The widget signs in as that key's client_email, and shows only the GA4 properties that email has been granted.

1. Open the Google Cloud console (console.cloud.google.com) and pick or create a project for the key.
2. Under APIs & Services → Library, enable the Google Analytics Data API and the Google Analytics Admin API.
3. Under IAM & Admin → Service accounts, create a service account. It needs no project role.
4. Open the new service account and choose Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON. A JSON file downloads.
5. Paste that whole file here.
6. In Google Analytics, open Admin → Property access management → Add users. Enter the key's client_email and choose Viewer.
7. Repeat step 6 on every property the widget should show. Use Property access management, not Account access management: the account-level grant attaches the email to only the first property in the account.
8. Quit the widget and start it again after a new grant. Refresh does not look for new properties.

A Google login that can see more properties does not add them; only what the key's email was granted is shown. The widget re-mints its hour-long token from the key on its own. When both credentials and credentials_file are set, this one wins. It is stored in config.json, which should be chmod 600, and is never shown again once written. Full steps: docs/google-setup.md.
google_analytics._credentials_file_comment:
Path to the service-account JSON key (~/ is expanded), used when credentials is empty.

1. Create the key and download it: steps 1 to 4 under credentials.
2. Save the file outside any repository, and run chmod 600 on it.
3. Enter its path here.
4. Grant the key's client_email Viewer on each property: steps 6 to 8 under credentials.

The screen warns when the file is readable by anyone but you. Full steps: docs/google-setup.md.
google_analytics._properties_comment: Numeric GA4 property ids - the number after p in GA's admin URLs. Empty lists every property the service account can see (Admin API account summaries).
google_analytics._realtime_refresh_comment:
Seconds between realtime readings of the property on screen: 120, 300 or 600; anything else means 120. The l key cycles them while running.

Other properties read every 300 s. It backs off to 300 s after 10 minutes at 0 active users, stretches when today's spend on the property by every pane and tool would empty its daily quota before midnight Pacific, and slows to 600 s under 10% of quota left; the title says which.
google_analytics._refresh_comment: Seconds between processed reports (hourly, sources, key events, movers, organic landing pages) for the property on screen: 1800, 3600 or 7200; at least 1800. GA's processed data is 2-6 hours behind, so faster gains nothing. A property off screen reads them when it is shown, if this long has passed.
google_analytics._window_days_comment: Days in the movers and organic landing page window, compared with the equal window before it. The w key cycles 7, 14 and 28.
google_analytics._baseline_weeks_comment: How many past weeks the realtime baseline is the median of. Samples older than this plus one week are pruned from the sample file.
google_analytics._key_events_comment: Event names to treat as key events, counted by event count. Empty uses every event GA flags as a key event.

google_search_console._comment: Google Search Console through a service-account key: hourly search traffic, the pages and queries that moved, the search terms that land on the site, URL Inspection of the pages that matter, and sitemaps. Read-only (webmasters.readonly). docs/google-setup.md is the Google side.
google_search_console._credentials_comment:
The service-account JSON key itself: paste the whole downloaded file here. The widget signs in as that key's client_email, and shows only the Search Console properties that email has been added to.

1. Open the Google Cloud console (console.cloud.google.com) and pick or create a project for the key.
2. Under APIs & Services → Library, enable the Google Search Console API.
3. Under IAM & Admin → Service accounts, create a service account. It needs no project role.
4. Open the new service account and choose Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON. A JSON file downloads.
5. Paste that whole file here.
6. In Search Console, pick a property, then Settings → Users and permissions → Add user. Enter the key's client_email and choose Restricted.
7. Repeat step 6 for every property the widget should show.

The widget re-mints its hour-long token from the key on its own. When both credentials and credentials_file are set, this one wins. It is stored in config.json, which should be chmod 600, and is never shown again once written. Full steps: docs/google-setup.md.
google_search_console._credentials_file_comment:
Path to the service-account JSON key (~/ is expanded), used when credentials is empty.

1. Create the key and download it: steps 1 to 4 under credentials.
2. Save the file outside any repository, and run chmod 600 on it.
3. Enter its path here.
4. In Search Console, add the key's client_email as a Restricted user under Settings → Users and permissions, on every property the widget should show.

A [!] notice warns when the file is readable by anyone but you. Full steps: docs/google-setup.md.
google_search_console._sites_comment: Properties exactly as Search Console names them: sc-domain:example.com for a domain property, or https://example.com/ with its trailing slash for a URL prefix. Empty reads every property the account can see.
google_search_console._refresh_comment: Seconds between reads of the site on screen's last 24 hours and daily totals, at least 300. Its pages, queries and terms are read when Google finalises another day, or every six hours; sites not on screen read only their daily totals, hourly.
google_search_console._window_days_comment: Complete days in each movers window, compared with the equal window before it. w switches between 7 and 28 while running.
google_search_console._inspect_top_comment:
How many pages from the movers answer are inspected once a day, the ones with the most impressions, plus as many that dropped to zero.

Search Analytics ranks by clicks and stops at 1,000; the INDEX HEALTH header says so when that cut the answer. 0 turns inspection off. Google allows 2,000 inspections a day per property.
google_search_console._search_type_comment: Which Google results to read: web, image, video, news or discover. t steps through them while running.

google_trends._comment: Google's Trending Now feed for one or more regions, read from trends.google.com/trending/rss with no account or key. Traffic is Google's bucket, shown as written; SEEN and LEFT THE FEED are this widget's own counts across fetches.
google_trends._geos_comment: Region codes to show, as Google's feed takes them in ?geo= - two-letter country codes such as "US", "GB", "JP". The first is shown at start; ←/→ steps through the rest. A code Google does not know is shown as rejected rather than dropped.
google_trends._refresh_comment: Seconds between fetches of each region's feed; minimum 60. Google refreshes the feed every few minutes, so faster polling shows nothing new.

latency._hosts_comment: Hostnames or addresses passed to ping; every target is measured independently. Anything ping accepts works — "1.1.1.1", "db1.internal", "example.com" — and a name that does not resolve shows as DOWN rather than being dropped, so a typo is visible instead of silent.
latency._interval_comment: Seconds between ping samples per target; minimum 1 second.
latency._seconds_per_column_comment: Seconds represented by one graph column; 0 chooses from the pane width and retained window.
latency._window_comment: Seconds of readings retained for statistics and graphs.
latency._spike_factor_comment: How many times above the recent baseline marks a latency spike.
latency._aggregate_comment: How several samples in one graph column are combined.
latency._strip_suffixes_comment:
Hostname suffixes removed from on-screen labels only — the target is still pinged by its full name.

Give the leading dot: ".internal" turns db1.internal into db1, and ".eu-west-1.compute.internal" turns a long cloud name into the host part. Longest match wins, so a general suffix and a more specific one can both be listed.

linear._comment: Personal API key: Linear Settings -> Security & access -> Personal API keys. Nothing needs selecting; exclude_teams is for dropping a noisy automated intake. Keep this file chmod 600.
linear._token_comment: Linear personal API key; leave empty to read the named environment variable.
linear._token_env_comment: Environment variable that holds the Linear API key.
linear._exclude_teams_comment: Linear team identifiers omitted from every aggregate.
linear._window_days_comment: Days included in issue and cycle trend charts.

link._comment: Every established connection into a port this machine listens on. Empty ports means all of them, which is the useful default. No network traffic: the numbers come from the kernel's own accounting via ss on Linux or nettop on macOS.
link._ports_comment: Listening ports counted as inbound sessions; empty uses every listening port.
link._history_comment: Minimum number of rate samples retained.
link._windows_comment: What w cycles the chart through, in seconds; the first is what opens. history is only a floor — retention follows the longest window on its own.

months._week_start_comment: Which day a week begins on. Sunday by default. It moves where the row breaks and nothing else: week numbers stay ISO 8601, which is Monday-reckoned whatever the grid does and says so on the pane, and the weekend stays Saturday and Sunday.
months._week_numbers_comment:
Whether the ISO 8601 week number is shown in a gutter down the left of each month. On by default.

Turning it off is not only a column back: a narrower month means more of them fit across the same pane. It is dropped on its own when the pane is too narrow for it and seven days both, because a week number is worth less than the seventh day of the week.
months._timezone_comment:
Which zone today is reckoned in, as an IANA name such as Asia/Tokyo. Empty is this machine's own zone, which is what clocks shows.

It matters because for several hours of every day it is a different date in two places, and the pane names whichever zone it used. A name the timezone database does not know falls back to this machine and says so on screen rather than quietly marking somebody else's today.

mux_activity._comment: What mux-activity reads: every pane of the multiplexer it runs in - Rex, Herdr or Luvus - through that multiplexer's CLI, read-only. A rex_panes, herdr_panes or luvus_panes section from before is read when there is no mux_activity section.
mux_activity._backend_comment: Which multiplexer to read. auto finds out from the pane mux-activity runs in: REX_SESSION and REX_BLOCK for Rex, HERDR_ENV=1 for Herdr, LUVUS_ENV=1 for Luvus, and the nearest of them in the process tree when several are set. The --mux flag overrides this.
mux_activity._rex_server_comment: Which Rex server to read: a host label from `rex hosts`, or an address. Empty means the CLI's own default - REX_SERVER when it is set, else this machine's server. Set, it is read from anywhere, inside a multiplexer or not. CPU and memory are shown only for this machine's server.
mux_activity._luvus_session_comment: Under Luvus, which Luvus server session to read. `luvus session list` names the ones on this machine; `default` is the one `luvus` starts on its own.
mux_activity._refresh_comment: Maximum idle delay in seconds; Rex events wake a full read sooner.
mux_activity._agents_comment: Under Rex, command names that count as coding agents; Herdr and Luvus name their agents themselves. Matched against the pane's foreground program, and against the app name a program reports with OSC 7501 (claude also matches a report from claude-code or claude-cli).

netwatch._comment: Which processes are using the network. Linux uses per-socket TCP counters from `ss` plus `/proc`; macOS uses all-protocol per-process counters from `nettop`. The pane names the active measurement. Totals start at zero each launch.
netwatch._interval_comment: Seconds between applied source samples. macOS nettop has a one-second minimum; redraw and selection remain independent.
netwatch._limit_comment: Maximum process rows; 0 means no configured limit.
netwatch._sort_comment: Initial ordering: total bytes or live rate.
netwatch._external_comment: Linux only: narrow socket rows to internet peers. macOS process totals have no peer field.
netwatch._mine_comment: Linux only: hide unattributed sockets initially. macOS nettop rows are already process-labelled.

ports._comment: What is listening on this machine. `o` hides the machine's own ports — every port another user owns, plus the extras named in system_ports. Reads /proc and ss on Linux or lsof, ps and nettop on macOS, plus `tailscale serve status` for the exposure column.
ports._system_ports_comment:
Extra ports to hide behind `o`, which hides them by default. Ports another user owns are hidden already, so this list only ever adds to them and can never reveal one.

It is for what is yours by uid and still not yours in spirit — a rootless sshd, a user-session mDNS responder. Empty hides none by port.
ports._refresh_comment: Seconds between listening-socket and traffic refreshes.

tailnet._comment_history: rate samples kept per peer; the chart is a window on to this
tailnet._refresh_comment: Seconds between Tailscale status and traffic refreshes.

vercel_deployments._comment: token: create one at Account Settings -> Tokens. The Vercel CLI's session is not used — it expires within hours. Keep this file chmod 600.
vercel_deployments._token_comment: Vercel account token; leave empty to read the named environment variable.
vercel_deployments._token_env_comment: Environment variable that holds the Vercel token.
vercel_deployments._teams_comment:
Vercel team identifiers to include. Leave it empty and every team the token can see is covered — the widget lists them itself on start, so a team you join appears without editing anything. Name teams here only to narrow it to those.

With no token the poller says so and makes no request; the personal account is what you get when a valid token can see no teams.

If listing them fails or stops early the board says so rather than quietly showing less.
vercel_deployments._projects_comment: Project identifiers to include; empty includes every project in scope.
